items.title: Digital Foundry offers a techincal review of Final Fantasy XIV on Switch 2
items.content:
0 It was a long time coming, but Square Enix finally released Final Fantasy XIV on Switch 2 this year. This is a popular and highly acclaimed MMO in the storied Final Fantasy franchise, now playable on Nintendo’s handheld console hybrid. Often with ports of big games like this one, the question is just how well they managed to get it running on the new hardware, and now we’ve got a video exploring that subject.

Digital Foundry has once again provided a technical review of a Switch 2 game, and this time it’s Final Fantasy XIV. This is a detailed analysis of the game’s framerate and image quality, as well as some special Switch 2 features. Their overall conclusion is that the game “absolutely can be a satisfying experience, but overall expectations should be kept modest.” See below for specific tidbits.

items.title: Final Fantasy 14 Is Bringing Back a Fan-Favorite Crossover for the First Time in Over Two Years
items.summary: Finally, another chance to get one of the best mounts in Square Enix's MMO
items.content:
By Willa Rowe Published Sep 18, 2026, 2:01 PM EDT Willa Rowe is a contributing writer at Polygon, covering games and entertainment. She is a New York-based journalist and critic whose work has been featured in Kotaku, Digital Trends, the A.V. Club, GamesRadar+, and more. She also co-hosts the Girl Mode podcast. News Finally, another chance to get one of the best mounts in Square Enix's MMO

Y'shtola is featured prominently in the Final Fantasy XIV: Shadowbringers trailer. Image: Square Enix Final Fantasy 14 Sign in to your Polygon.com account Add Us Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap It's official, Noctis is returning to Eorzea. Square Enix has officially announced that the Nocturne for Heroes event will once again be available in Final Fantasy 14 for a limited time. Players last experienced the Final Fantasy 15 crossover in 2024.

Warriors of Light can pick up the quest that begins the crossover starting on Sept. 24, 2026 at 1:00 a.m. PDT. You'll have just a few weeks to complete it and collect all of the collaboration's rewards, as the event concludes on Oct. 13, 2026 at 7:59 a.m. PDT. The Nocturne for Heroes event first ran in 2021 and returned in 2024, so don't expect that you'll be able to play it again anytime soon after this year's revival concludes. The quest line for the event sees the Warrior of Light aiding Noctis, the protagonist of Final Fantasy 15 .

Players can start the event by picking up the quest "The Man in Black" from Kipih Jakkya in Ul'dah near the Steps of Nald. If you've previously completed the quests, you can speak to the NPC to use the seasonal event replay feature. You won't be able to start the event unless you have a character that is level 50, and you've completed the main scenario quest, "The Ultimate Weapon."

It seems like somebody didn’t get the memo Square Enix via Polygon There will, of course, be plenty of limited-time items to collect during the event. The hottest item will be the Regalia Type-G mount , which continues to be one of the MMO's best mounts. It'll cost 200,000 MGP from the Ironworks Vendor. But that won't be the only reward to grab. Here's a full list of items and how to get them.

If this isn't your first time doing the event, you might try playing it on the Switch 2; It may unexpectedly be the best place to play the MMO .

Congrats on beating Dancing Mad (Ultimate), it was easier before patch 7.55

items.title: Inside Final Fantasy XIV’s Evercold Expansion with Koji Fox and Toshio Murouchi
Next Final Fantasy FFXIV Crossover Brings FFXV Back
items.summary: Noctis from FFXV will back in FFXIV for a time thanks to the return of a limited-time crossover event quest.
items.content:
FFXIV will get content from another Final Fantasy game again thanks to a rerun of the FFXV crossover. Square Enix announced that will kick off next week on September 24, 2026. This run of A Nocturne for Heroes is identical to the event that first debuted back in April 2019 , so there’s nothing new if you already met Noctis Lucis Caelum. However, this does mark the first time the event appeared since the launch of the Switch 2 release.

As usual, the requirements for the questline that begins with “ The Man in Black ” are a bit high compared to some of these crossovers or special events. You must get your character to level 50 and have finished the A Realm Reborn main scenario quest “The Ultimate Weapon.” If you have, then Kipih Jakkya will be at Ul’dah, Steps of Nald at X:8.5, Y:9.7. This starts a three-quest storyline that results in someone getting the Regalia Type-G mount and the Lucian Prince’s armor set that features boots, bottoms, a fingerless glove, and a jacket. Someone can also unlock Noctis’ Lucian Locks Modern Aesthetics hairstyle for finishing it.

Here’s the original trailer that goes over the event.

This marks the fourth time we’ve seen this FFXV crossover quest in FFXIV . Following the 2019 debut, it returned in 2021 and 2024 as well. This also means that this time every single platform the game is on will get a chance to go over it again.

Final Fantasy XIV is available for the Switch 2, PS4, PS5, Xbox Series X, and PC. Final Fantasy XV is on the PS4, Xbox One, and PC via the standard version and Switch, PS4, Xbox One, PC, and mobile devices via the Pocket Edition. The FFXIV FFXV crossover event returns between September 24, 2026 and October 13, 2026.

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV Is A Place People Call Home, And The Rising Proves It
items.summary: The Rising asks Final Fantasy XIV's community to remember. The community's answers are about loss, connection, and the people they found in the game.
items.content:
Square Enix By Linda Güster Published Sep 16, 2026, 12:00 PM EDT Linda Güster is a Contributor at DualShockers and a German, UK-based gaming journalist specializing in video games, esports, industry analysis, features, lists, reviews, interviews, and news. She has been writing professionally since 2020 and began covering video games and esports in 2025, turning a lifelong passion into her professional focus.

Before joining DualShockers, Linda worked as content lead for Esports Insider DACH and The Escapist Magazine Germany . She previously worked in software engineering and digital media, giving her a strong technical background and the ability to explain complex systems clearly. Across her career, she has written thousands of news pieces and covered gaming culture, esports, technology, and broader industry developments.

There's a moment every year in Final Fantasy XIV that feels different from everything else the game offers. The Rising, which ran this year from August 27 to September 11, is officially an anniversary event – a celebration of A Realm Reborn's relaunch, where the people of Eorzea pay tribute to those lost in the Seventh Umbral Calamity. In practice, for the community that has built its life around this game, it tends to become something more personal than that. It becomes a mirror. A moment to look back at how far you've come, what you've carried with you, and who you've brought along.

If you've ever concerned yourself with the best Final Fantasy stories from the games, I encourage you to look at our ranking of the mainline series.

I've written before about how MMORPGs fill a gap that modern life has made harder to fill – the gap left by the kinds of communities that used to form more naturally, in the spaces between work and obligation. Final Fantasy XIV has become one of the most remarkable examples of a game doing exactly that. The Rising is the point in the year when that becomes most visible, and the community responses the EU Community Discord provided make that clearer than anything I could say myself.

The Rising exists because Final Fantasy XIV has a history worth commemorating. A Realm Reborn's relaunch in 2013 followed the near-total failure of version 1.0, and the decision to essentially rebuild the game from the ground up rather than walk away from it produced something that became more than a recovery story. It became the foundation for a game that has, over more than a decade, accumulated layers of meaning that most live service games never come close to.

The event itself – city-states decorated, side stories on the Lodestone, the Wandering Minstrel as its recurring anchor, Naoki Yoshida himself woven into its narrative – treats its own history with a reverence that players have picked up and reflected back. This year's rewards included the Wind-up Wuk Lamat minion, furnishings carrying the Rising's branding across multiple years, and a set of orchestrion rolls that spanned the franchise's history from Matoya's Cave to Zanarkand. Even the reward structure tells you a lot about what the event is for.

Various members of the EU Community Discord responded to an inquiry about the anniversaries they hold dear in Final Fantasy XIV, and the responses painted a picture of a game that has embedded itself into people's lives in ways that go well beyond gameplay milestones.

J started playing on the day Patch 5.3 launched and has since come to think of The Rising as their character's anniversary – a fitting overlap, given what the event is for. "I like the opportunity to recall my feelings playing through MSQ for the first time," they told us. "For The Rising I really like the way the theme of 'remembering the fallen' is handled. It feels like something of a reset and fresh start. It's really cathartic." Sometimes they use New Game+ to replay Main Scenario Quest content on expansion anniversaries too, a ritual of return that the game's design makes unusually easy.

Not everyone marks time through the game's own calendar. Sarah's character has a birthday that was never logged by the system – she gave her one herself, her father's birthday, February 23. "Without him, I wouldn't be here," she said. It's a small thing, an in-character date that means nothing to anyone else in Eorzea, but it's the kind of personalization that speaks to how deeply people have made this world their own. About a year ago, Sarah also built a small community from scratch that gathered every day for six months before gradually dispersing into smaller groups – and she's since heard that at least one of those groups ended up together romantically.

Ease into a different genre with these cozy titles that will be perfect for RPG fans.

The communities people form tend to outlast the content that brought them together. Pine joined in August 2020 and keeps track of that month every year, but what she actually celebrates are raid tier clears – not just her own, but the ones her original static members reach in their new groups long after the static itself dispersed. "All but one are in different statics now, but we keep in touch and when everyone is done we hop on a call to hang out and discuss how it was for us and our groups," she said. Hailey has done something similar with Free Company anniversaries, gathering at the FC house when everyone can manage it. "It's rare that everybody gets together like that," she told us. "Even if it doesn't feel like it in the moment, it's these kinds of moments that we remember for a long time."

Some of the fondest memories have nothing to do with progression at all. Koneko has been playing since 2014, when her character was created with one black eye and one white, named Lockheart because it was the first game that ever asked for a surname. She still has a screenshot from that year of a Scholar fight where Eos actively ran away from her mid-battle. "I still have the screenshot of it happening with the reactions of my friends who all saw me question my sanity," she said. Her actual fondest memory is even simpler: the first time she played with a friend who thought a pugilist was a tank because of Feather Fall. Taya's fondest memory is twenty people sitting in a pool in A Realm Reborn, a dice-drinking game, nothing but laughs and positivity. Tommie's answer to the fondest memory question was the shortest of anyone's, and also among the most complete: finally meeting his fiancé in-game.

It became the foundation for a game that has, over more than a decade, accumulated layers of meaning that most live service games never come close to.

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV: Complete Edition for Nintendo Switch 2 Review
items.summary: FINAL FANTASY XIV Online Complete Edition is perfect for new players as it includes the base game and all expansions through Dawntrail.
items.content:
Final Fantasy XIV released on the Switch 2 as of a few weeks ago (depending on date of publication). I bought the Complete Edition , which gives access through Dawntrail … without knowing about the impending free trial version due out on August 4th. Still, I got 2 months+ worth of playtime to work with before having to get a Switch 2-specific subscription. So, how does it fare so far just after the A Realm Reborn expansion? Let’s find out!

Now, if you’re a Switch 2 newbie (like I am), then a lot of what is mentioned here will appear overwhelming to you, especially the plot of A Realm Reborn . Though, don’t worry, you do not need to play FFXIV 1.0 to understand FFXIV: A Realm Reborn ’s story, though having prior knowledge will help in understanding the context of certain flashbacks.You see, those masked individuals working with the Ixal (if your hometown is New Gridinia, more on that later) and in mysterious flashback cutscenes detailing the Primal Bahamut Dalahmud Moon that brought about the end of 1.0 are Ascions, aka: Paragons.

Their ability to summon creatures and possess people comes into play throughout A Realm Reborn and later expansions, and if you stick with it through all this story (there’s so much and constantly more coming into 2027 and beyond with Evercold ), you’ll discover the conflict between the Ascions and the Scions of the Seventh Dawn, with so many implications and events following these that I DARE not spoil. Yda and Papalymo are the first two story-significant characters you’ll meet, as a heads-up.

One of the downsides of Final Fantasy XIV: Complete Edition on Switch 2 is the need to pay a separate subscription fee entirely separate from the NOT-REQUIRED Switch Online. Yeah, in addition to needing any version of the game to play, nearly 150 GBs on space on your internal storage or MicroSD Express card, you also need a SEPARATE subscription to play the game past the free month grace period on Switch 2!! Yes, it’s annoying. Does it take away from the fun I am having right now? Hmm… a little. Thankfully, paying that fee is a bit easier than I thought. Just use the Nintendo eShop.

The game shines with its Xenoblade Chronicles -esque approach to combat. Each attack is on a cooldown after use. The more beneficial an attack or buff is, the longer it takes to recharge. Which attack you follow up with in combat after the previous one can offer benefits like increased damage to an enemy, for example, with the Lancer\Dragoon’s True Thrust following the use of a vorpal blade.

On the performance side of the gameplay, when dealing with less than 8 NPCs in one area at a time, like in a city or overworld, the FPS is generally 60, for BOTH docked and handheld (I don’t care about FPS as long as it’s stable and PLAYABLE). In the city or certain intense areas, the FPS is at a steady 30.

The music as always is excellent. the theme that capped off 1.0, known as “Answers”, is the most beautiful and best song in the entire franchise. Playing mainly in the raid dungeon known as The Unending Coil of Bahamut (Ultimate)’s final battle against Primal Bahamut, this song is masterclass in orchestral majestic bliss, and so on and so forth. I have listened to it about 50 times so far, with each time better than the last. It also plays at one other important point in the expansions that I, again, DARE not spoil, by the way.

And there’s so much more I even haven’t gotten into. Side quests, Raid Battles, FATE Battles, Team compositions for Raid dungeons, Parties, etc. AND, lastly, did I mention I’m STILL on the first expansion ( A Realm Reborn )?! I’m just now checking out the other two towns and their overworlds as part of the larger quest. AND I still have SIX more expansions after this to get through! There’s certainly a LOT of content here, which I can appreciate, but there might be TOO MUCH for me to do in such a short time.

If you’re looking for a Xenoblade -type MMORPG with memorable characters and plenty of engaging story beats to keep you interested, this game will scratch that itch, and then some.

My one complaint is the number of expansions and the amount of story/side content is a bit too overbearing and hand-holdy at times. Other than that, I enjoyed my time with FFXIV and the realm of Eorzea, and I can’t wait to come back for another adventure with the Evercold expansion in 2027.

If you liked this review, be sure to check out my review on Legacy of Kain: Ascendance . Thanks for reading, and I’ll see you next time.

items.title: New ‘Final Fantasy 14’ Job Leaked on Square Enix’s Official Site
Square Enix reminds Final Fantasy XIV players that the Switch 2’s free subscription period is ending soon
items.summary: Square Enix posted an update on its official Final Fantasy XIV page today to remind players that the free one-month grace period for its long-running MMO on
items.content:
Square Enix posted an update on its official Final Fantasy XIV page today to remind players that the free one-month grace period for its long-running MMO on Switch 2 will be ending soon. Starting September 7th, 2026, players will either need to buy the “Starter” or “Complete” editions of the game, or switch over to the free-trial that limits access to certain features. If you’ve already purchased FFXIV on Switch 2, your included month of game access will take effect on September 8, 2026.

This can be a little confusing to those not familiar with MMOs, but Square Enix launched FFXIV on Switch 2 with 30 free days as a means of testing the server stability on Nintendo’s console. Technically speaking, the game doesn’t actually release until September 7th, so Square Enix wants to remind players that they’ll soon need to start paying to keep playing. MMO fees go towards server maintenance and the development of additional content, of which Final Fantasy XIV has received six major expansion packs, so this isn’t anything new. This announcement is merely a warning so that people aren’t caught off guard if they suddenly lose access.

In order to pay for access on Nintendo Switch 2, players will need to utilize FFXIV coins, as Square Enix calls them. This is a separate subscription from the PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S versions, though having dual subscriptions will net you a 50% discount for access on the Switch 2 port. Basically, you purchase coins ahead of time and use those to pay off the monthly fee. FFXIV coins can be purchased from the game’s launcher, which will redirect to the eShop for completion of the purchase. It seems a little convoluted, but I suppose Square Enix is trying to conform to standards set by Nintendo’s online ecosystem.

If you don’t want to deal with any of that, Final Fantasy XIV does have a rather generous free trial. You’re limited in certain aspects, such as losing the ability to form parties with other players, but you can otherwise experience the entirety of XIV’s story and even play through the first four expansions. It’s certainly a hell of a lot of content for the low price of $0.

The range features graphic hoodies, character tees, washed denim sets and Mothercrystal jewelry.

Launches September 16, 2026, via Tokyo pop-ups and Diesel online.

Diesel has teamed up with Square Enix ‘s acclaimed MMORPG Final Fantasy XIV for a multi-faceted project anchored in the shared philosophy of “BRAVE”.

Fusing fashion, gaming culture and contemporary art, the centerpiece of the project is a 27-piece capsule collection. The lineup translates rich gaming lore into streetwear staples, spanning washed denim jackets, wide-leg denim trousers, hoodies, long-sleeve tees, graphic T-shirts and silver jewelry. Design motifs draw directly from the world of Hydaelyn, featuring imagery of Azem’s Crystal, the Mothercrystal, the Grand Companies of Eorzea and iconic Scions of the Seventh Dawn characters including Y’shtola, Thancred, Alphinaud, and Estinien.

Ranging in price from ¥11,000 to ¥207,900 JPY (approx. $69 – $1,302 USD), the collection kicks off on September 16, 2026, with an exclusive pop-up at Isetan Shinjuku in Tokyo, which will offer custom job-icon embroidery services and a 30-set limited “Scions of the Seventh Dawn Complete Box”. A wider release follows on October 2, 2026, via Diesel’s official online store and the DIESEL SHIBUYA flagship, alongside secondary pop-ups at Hankyu Umeda in Osaka and Iwataya in Fukuoka later in the month. Coinciding with the drop, DIESEL ART GALLERY in Shibuya will host a collaborative collage art exhibition by renowned artist Kosuke Kawamura from October 2 through November 8, 2026. items.title: Final Fantasy XIV is perfect for the Switch 2
items.summary: Though it has its ups and downs
items.content:
Final Fantasy XIV coming to the Switch 2 is a dream come true for me; one of my favorite games now in a portable form factor. I’ve put a ton of time into the game on the system, testing just about every scenario I can think of outside of becoming a streamer and having a crowd of people follow me everywhere. Overall, I’m pretty happy with the port and can recommend it to players new and old, but I certainly wouldn’t abandon PC for this version.

The thing I and most others were curious about most was performance on Switch 2. I have bad news on that front, as you’re pretty much never going to get 60 frames per second on Switch 2 outside of certain cutscenes and exactly one area in one dungeon. It’s disappointing there’s no performance mode or anything, but you can cap your framerate to 30 in Docked Mode for more stability. Portable is also capped at 30, so you’re essentially getting parity with that aside from resolution. Your framerate can and will still dip below 30 in some situations, like running around a crowded Limsa Lominsa, but Limsa ‘tis a silly place. You can hear more about performance in this short:

As for visuals, the game looks good. Not amazing; there’s a lot of aliasing, and you can definitely tell the resolution is lower when going from 1440p or 4K on PC, but good. Resolution often screws with your custom HUD setup, which is something I was worried about here, but aside from needing to increase the chatbox font and move my job gauges a bit to the right, I was able to download my configs no problem. It moves seamlessly between portable and docked modes as well, something this version has over playing the PC version on Steam Deck.

Steam Deck might be able to hit higher framerates more consistently, but Switch 2 has it soundly beat in convenience and battery life, not to mention fan noise. I gave up playing the game on Steam Deck after Dawntrail launched, as just playing the game made my Deck scream in agony and it would go from full battery to almost dead very, very quickly. That’s at the lowest possible settings and with a lower resolution than Switch 2 offers. FFXIV will still drain the Switch 2 pretty quickly, but it’s far from the worst I’ve seen on the platform. Just make sure you don’t register for a duty at like 30% battery and you’re fine, or have your docked setup nearby.

Being able to go from portable to docked seamlessly here is fantastic, though the star of the show here really is portable mode. I love being able to do my dailies and slowly get every Job to cap while sitting on my couch, talking with my family, or just not sitting at my PC. Especially with the weather being so hot and my bedroom, where my computer lives, is basically an oven. I could even play outside on the porch if going outside wouldn’t melt me.

One of the best parts of portable mode is the touch screen. Sometimes navigating certain menus is just more convenient with a mouse-like setup, and just being able to touch the screen makes it super easy. In Docked mode, you can use either one of the Joy-Con 2 as a mouse, but I find this feature leaves a lot to be desired; both when you’re using it and even when you’re not. Playing with split Joy-Con 2, I found my fingers would often activate the mouse sensor, messing up my controls for a second or two. Playing with mouse mode… You just don’t have enough buttons to actually play the game unless you’re the kind of person who likes to click on their hotbar actions. You could plug in a Keyboard and just use one of the Joy-Con 2 as a mouse, which does allow for a left-handed mouse setup, but at that point you might as well just plug in an actual MMO mouse while you’re at it.

Another point of contention is that there’s no physical release. That’s not a big deal for Final Fantasy XIV as it hasn’t actually been on a disc in a long time, but on Switch 2 storage space is at a premium. Final Fantasy XIV will take up almost half of your console’s onboard storage at 108 GB. With Evercold on the Horizon, it’s only going to get bigger too. I actually bought a new microSD card specifically for this game, and am working on putting together a faux physical copy, complete with a game box and “cartridge” to store the SD card in. With… everything getting so expensive lately, I settled on a 256 GB card, so I’ll have to swap out the SD card to play my other Switch 2 games, which is inconvenient. You could simply keep FFXIV on your onboard storage and all other games on an SD card, which was recommended when the game launched as there were loading issues with the SD card, but I prefer to have at least some variety.

As of writing and most likely as of when you read this, Square Enix is offering all Switch 2 players a free month of the game. After that ends, you’ll need to pay an additional subscription fee to play on Switch 2 and other platforms like PC and PS5. If you just play on Switch 2, you simply pay the normal sub, but if, for example, you want to swap between PC and Switch 2 you’ll have to pay an additional half of the subscription each month. This is done through a weird currency obfuscation method Square Enix calls FFXIV Coins. You buy coins, then use them to pay for the sub.

First off, why the obfuscation? I’d really rather you just tell me up front what it costs without me having to translate and convert. There’s a reason Nintendo and Microsoft got rid of their points systems on their storefronts. Second, I know this is how Square got out of requiring players to need Nintendo Switch Online to play on Switch 2… but personally I already pay for NSO every year, and it’s overall cheaper than this weird Coin model; $50 a year for the Expansion Pak version as opposed to $70 a year by my math. That $70 doesn’t include an already existing subscription to FFXIV, by the way; that’s just on top of playing on Switch 2. I haven’t actually paid for my sub in a long time (thanks for literally paying my sub, Square!), but if I were to stop writing about FFXIV, I would be concerned about that additional cost. Being subscribed to NSO does get you an additional free teleport destination in-game… but I have teleport tickets; I don’t need that. It’s quite literally useless to me. In this situation, I’d probably just pick what I’m going to play on for that month: Switch 2 or PC.

Seeing as the Switch 2 version feels more like a nice supplement to me, I’d go with PC most of the time. In between MSQ patches, sure, I’ll take Switch 2, but if I go back to raiding or when there’s more story to play, I’d prefer the higher fidelity and framerate of my PC. I hope Square and Nintendo reconsider the choice of FFXIV Coin, because if they did, I’d shill this version as much as humanly possible. I mean, I’ll still do that for the game overall, but here I’d mostly recommend the free trial, then moving over to PC or being absolutely sure you want to play on Switch 2 forever. If FFXIV Coin wasn’t a thing, then you’d bet your sweet bippy I’d buy every expansion twice (read: once, thanks again Square!) so I could play on both platforms. For right now though, I’m pretty dang happy with this version.

items.content:
Summer is here once more, with fireworks lighting the night sky and festive decorations adorning the streets below. The sandy shores of Costa del Sol offer the perfect respite from the sweltering heat, so it’s time to dive right in and make a splash at the Moonfire Faire!

Event Duration

From Wednesday, August 12, 2026 at 1:00 a.m. (PDT) / 8:00 (GMT) / 9:00 (BST) / 18:00 (AEST) to Wednesday, August 26, 2026 at 7:59 a.m. (PDT) / 14:59 (GMT) / 15:59 (BST) / Thursday, 27 August at 0:59 (AEST)

How to Participate

Begin the quest "Earning Your Water Wings" by speaking to Mayaru Moyaru in Limsa Lominsa, Upper Deck (X:11.5 Y:13.8). * Players must be level 30 and above to start the quest.

Rewards

* Certain items available during previous iterations of the event can be purchased via Moonfire Faire vendors. Visit the special site for more details.

items.title: Gather One, Gather All─Yo-kai Watch Returns to Eorzea!
items.summary: Once more, a horde of Yo-kai descends upon Eorzea! Join in the fun and get your paws on weapons, mounts, a framer's kit, and minions─including Jibanyan and Whisper! This time around, the event features three new indoor furnishings: wibbly-w
items.content:
Once more, a horde of Yo-kai descends upon Eorzea! Join in the fun and get your paws on weapons, mounts, a framer's kit, and minions─including Jibanyan and Whisper! This time around, the event features three new indoor furnishings: wibbly-wobbly Jibanyan, wibbly-wobbly Komasan, and wibbly-wobbly USApyon. * This event is identical to the one previously held, with the addition of three indoor furnishing items. * If you have already completed the quest for this event, it cannot be accepted again. However, you may still earn Yo-kai Medals while equipped with a Yo-kai Watch. * During the event, Yo-kai Watches will be available for purchase from recompense officers in major cities.

Event Duration

From Tuesday, August 4, 2026 at 1:00 a.m. (PDT) / 8:00 (GMT) / 9:00 (BST) / 18:00 (AEST) to Monday, October 5, 2026 at 7:59 a.m. (PDT) / 14:59 (GMT) / 15:59 (BST) / Tuesday, 6 October at 1:59 (AEDT) * Dates and times are subject to change.

How to Participate

Speak with the poor-heeled youth on the Steps of Nald (X:9.2 Y:9.1) in Ul'dah. Upon completion of the quest, you will receive a Yo-kai Watch and Yo-kai Medallium which you can use to obtain Yo-kai Medals. * Players must be level 15 and above to start the quest. * Players must have completed one of the following main scenario quests: "The Gridanian Envoy," "The Lominsan Envoy," or "The Ul’dahn Envoy." Don't miss out on this zany collaboration event!

Rewards

Visit the special site for more details.
